labels: OWNER campaign approvals for the live PMUS spring probe. A campaign starts ONLY from an entry here whose campaign_id the durable campaign state has not run yet, after the previous campaign is complete and the continuation preflight (every filled market settled with venue-confirmed realized, zero open orders, positions flat) passes. Nothing here changes a per-market cap, the residual cap, concurrency, maker/post-only, the fee-safe completion rule, the deadman, the daily-loss stop or the frozen fidelity gate.

L5 residual envelope (analysis/l5/l5_residual_risk.json, 2,216 windows): unmatched exposure in every window, held to settlement in 98.96%, win rate 0.4993, residual P&L -$19,963 -- a coin flip that loses; at material size peak unmatched was 10.8-13.7% of deployed capital, which at our $7.50 cap is $1.03, below one action, so one action ($2.50) is the tightest implementable dollar cap. The live selection that chose the losing R3L market carried pair_at_touch 0.99, above the 0.98 bound, and every later decision logged complement_not_priceable; the measured maker rebate (0.808% of filled dollars, $0.0033/share) pays for a pair up to ~1.003, so par is the evidence-backed ceiling and the owner's guardrail makes it HARD.

approvals.source: OWNER chat 2026-09-11. Asked whether to keep shadowing or go live, the owner answered: 'is this just a shadow or should we be seeing real money involved', then 'can we just use real money now so we can get the rebates and see if that works?', then chose option 3 of the three offered -- 'go 3' -- which was stated to him as: 'Go live now with a q=1 canary at a relaxed target -- skips the shadow confirmation, accepts a ceiling change on mechanical reasoning rather than measured fill rates.' Asked which target, he selected 'Join the touch, hard cap <=1.00'. He reaffirmed 'go 3' a second time while this row was being written. STANDING CONSTRAINTS CARRIED IN FROM THE SAME DAY, none of them revoked: 'Keep the daily stop at -$15. It did exactly what we wanted.' 'Do not count wba-saw or 1win-nemi as realized until venue cashflow is actually confirmed. Keep the derived values separate.' 'prepare -- but do not arm without approval -- a q=1 bounded live canary'. 'No same-side extension after a stranded first leg unless separately evidence-supported.' 'Preserve explicit SHADOW / TRADE_THROUGH_PROXY semantics; never call these fills or realized P&L.'
approvals.rung_derivation: THE RUNG IS R5F HONOURING ITS OWN APPROVAL TEXT, not a new policy. The 2026-09-07 R5F approval reads 'L5-touch COMPLETE pricing; above-par pair cost is reported/accounted, not behaviorally gated', but R5F carries pair_cost_max: None, which falls through to DEFAULT_PAIR_COST_MAX = 0.98 at src/pmus_l5_ramp_ladder.py:295. So R5F has never run as approved. MEASURED ON THE LIVE PROBE, not inferred: across 2,382 complement preflight rows, pair_cost_max is 0.98 on 2,215, 1.00 on 33, None on 134; opp_ask - chosen_px is exactly 0.02 on 2,258 of them. We open as maker at our own side's touch (entry_px + opp_ask == 1.0000 on 2,279 of 2,371 filled opens, every one labelled touch_join), so pair-at-touch = 1 - spread, and on the 0.005-spread sports books that is 0.995. A 0.98 target is therefore arithmetically unreachable from the front of the queue: it pins the complement about three ticks back. Execution-shadow trade-through at that distance is 0.74%, against 47.6% at two ticks; live NFL examples carry 203,519 (bal-ind), 178,432 (chi-car) and 143,537 (atl-pit) shares ahead of us. L5 himself is 83.4% maker with a median pair of 0.9876, and 37.2% of his own pairs are above par and would be refused outright by the engine built to copy him. R5FT states the ceiling explicitly at par instead of inheriting 0.98, and shrinks every other lever to a one-market canary. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, on the face of the row: CLAUDE.md locks near-$1 pair tolerance to later incentive-era L5 unless equivalent economics are source-confirmed for our account, and our measured credit is $0.0134 per filled order with L5's own incentive economics unestablished. The two readings -- a deliberate lock versus an unintended default -- are recorded here rather than resolved by the engine. The canary exists to produce the fill and residual evidence that decides between them.
approvals.stop_rule_reading: ONE MARKET. markets_per_campaign is 1, so the campaign stops at the advance gate after a single market fills and settles; it also stops earlier at the -$15.00 daily realized-loss stop or the campaign horizon. Worst case per campaign is $3.00 of capital at risk on one market, with at most 4 actions at a $1.00 target and a $1.50 per-leg bound. The day already carries -$9.3736 venue-confirmed realized against the -$15.00 stop, so roughly $5.63 of loss budget remains before the stop refuses the next session -- checked before every session, and the canary's $3.00 worst case sits inside it. NO AUTOMATIC REPEAT: a completed or crashed bounded session does not relaunch itself, and the campaign is never auto-restarted after this gate.
approvals.changed: (1) pair_cost_max is STATED at 1.00 rather than inherited as 0.98, so the complement may join the best non-crossing maker price instead of resting three ticks behind it; par remains a hard floor (a rung asking for more still reads 1.00). (2) size is cut to a canary: per-market cap $7.50 -> $3.00, per-action target $2.50 -> $1.00, per-leg max -> $1.50, actions per session 6 -> 4, markets per campaign continuous -> 1, campaigns per day -> 1.
